_meta.indication: DALIRESP is indicated as a treatment to reduce the risk of COPD exacerbations in patients with severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations.
_meta.receipt_date: July 17, 2009 (original NDA); complete response resubmission received 08-30-2010

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of roflumilast 500 mcg once daily vs placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 40 years with severe COPD (FEV1 ≤ 50% predicted) associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of COPD exacerbation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 and rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations
pivotal_trials.result: Exacerbation rate 1.1 (roflumilast) vs 1.3 (placebo), rate ratio 0.85, p=0.028; pre-bronchodilator FEV1 improvement of 39 mL (46 vs 8 mL, p<0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of roflumilast 500 mcg once daily vs placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 40 years with severe COPD (FEV1 ≤ 50% predicted) associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of COPD exacerbation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints: change from baseline in pre-bronchodilator FEV1 and rate of moderate or severe COPD exacerbations
pivotal_trials.result: Exacerbation rate 1.2 (roflumilast) vs 1.5 (placebo), rate ratio 0.82, p=0.004; pre-bronchodilator FEV1 improvement of 58 mL (33 vs -25 mL, p<0.001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥2% and greater than placebo): diarrhea 9.5%, weight decreased 7.5%, nausea 4.7%, headache 4.4%. Psychiatric adverse reactions occurred in 5.9% of DALIRESP patients vs 3.3% placebo.
target_moa: Roflumilast and its active metabolite (roflumilast N-oxide) are selective inhibitors of phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4); inhibition leads to accumulation of intracellular cyclic AMP.

rems.type: FDA determined that a REMS is not necessary for DALIRESP Tablets to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (April 7, 2010): voted favorably on substantial evidence of efficacy (9 yes, 6 no) and safety profile (9 yes, 6 no), but against approvability (5 yes, 10 no).

description.text: Labeling update incorporating data from postmarketing commitment study (ROF-MD-07, RESPOND) and Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule; no new indication added

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to the prescribing information for Daliresp to incorporate data from the post marketing commitment study (ROF-MD-07, RESPOND) listed in the approval letter dated February 28, 2011, for Daliresp (roflumilast), and updating the prescribing information to meet the requirement of the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule.

description.text: Added a 250 mcg starting-dose up-titration regimen (250 mcg once daily for 4 weeks, then 500 mcg) to improve tolerability

citations.quote: This supplement also provides for the introduction of a roflumilast 250 mcg tablet to support a starting dose of 250 mcg once daily for the first 4 weeks followed by an increase to the roflumilast maintenance dosage of 500 mcg once daily.

summary.text: Roflumilast, a new molecular entity oral PDE4 inhibitor, was reviewed as a standard 505(b)(1) NDA. The original application received a Complete Response action (May 2010); after an advisory committee meeting and a complete response resubmission (received 08-30-2010) addressing the deficiencies, the NDA was approved.

citations.quote: Roflumilast is a new molecular entity that belongs to a class called phosphodiesterase type-4 (PDE-4) inhibitor.
Forest Pharmaceuticals originally submitted this 505(b)(1) application on July 15, 2009, for use of roflumilast tablets 500 mcg
Forest Pharmaceuticals submitted this complete response on August 30, 2010, satisfactorily addressing these deficiencies.

requirement.text: 1738-1: Conduct a controlled clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of roflumilast as an add-on therapy to a long-acting beta agonist and inhaled corticosteroid fixed-dose combination therapy in the indicated COPD population.

citations.quote: 1738-1 Conduct a controlled clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy of roflumilast as an add-on therapy to a long-acting beta agonist and inhaled corticosteroid fixed-dose combination therapy in the population of COPD patients for which roflumilast is indicated [severe COPD (FEV1 < 50% predicted) associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations].
FDA provided a complete response memorandum on 27 May 2010 stating that further evaluations were required before approval
